Bolhrad Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bolhrad, Ukraine

Not demolished. Founded no later than the second half of the 19th century, this cemetery appears on 1923 Russian maps using 1870s data and remains operational today. Jews faced expulsion efforts under Ottoman rule in Bolhrad from 1856-1878; the community maintained a cemetery and Talmud Torah by the 19th century's second half. Population reached 1,196 (10%) by 1897; the Birkut Holim society began in 1903, followed by a Jewish library in 1904, with three synagogues operating by 1910. Self-defense detachments formed 1918-1920, with the community also supplying weapons to units in nearby Tarutino. A Hebrew school and various Jewish party departments operated through the 1920s-30s; population reached 1,222 by 1930. Romanian occupation from July 20, 1941 killed 400 Jews within days; on September 2, 1941, nearly 140 men were shot while 363 women and children were interned before October deportation to Transnistria. A 1959 Holocaust memorial with Hebrew epigraph honors the victims.
